candidate.title: T-WGBS
candidate.scope: Tagmentation-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (T-WGBS), specifically the middle row of the assigned Illumina schematic: methylated-DNA input, methylated-adapter transposome tagmentation, oligo displacement and methylated replacement with gap repair, bisulfite conversion, and PCR to DNA. The adjacent EpiRADseq and JBP1-seq rows and partial chemical legend are context, with no depicted route into T-WGBS. No alternative T-WGBS version is shown. The separate catalogue page is a verified secondary match; detailed architecture is supported at schematic/catalogue level, while the supplied Wang primary-paper evidence is abstract-only.

evidence.rationale: The page reports bisulfite treatment followed by PCR and sequencing, C-to-T conversion of unmethylated cytosines, and single-base methylation resolution. Together these establish that converted genomic-insert sequence carries the modification readout into the amplified library. Thus the final DNA library represents the original modification pattern through sequence, not by requiring the native covalent methyl groups to remain on PCR products. The explicit 5mC/5hmC limitation restricts interpretation of protected cytosines.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Tn5 acts on the genomic DNA while delivering methylated adapter cargo, producing fragmented DNA with sequencing-adapter ends in one tagmentation step.
operations.mechanism: A hyperactive Tn5 transposase fragments DNA and appends sequencing adapters; the drawn transposome supplies the methylated adapters.
operations.information_effect: Genome-derived fragments carry their genomic sequence and preconversion modification state forward while acquiring adapter interfaces. The transposome supplies a reagent and catalytic activity, rather than a separate measurement branch.

operations.label: Displace oligo / Hybridize methylated adaptor and gap repair
operations.description: The tagged DNA undergoes oligonucleotide displacement, then hybridization of the supplied methylated replacement oligo and gap repair. The retained output is adapter-completed DNA; the displaced oligo is a separate, uncontinued output.
operations.mechanism: The depicted coupled block replaces an oligonucleotide and repairs the tagmented DNA to ensure methylated adapter addition. No displacement enzyme or detailed repair recipe is assigned.
operations.information_effect: Establishes the methylated adapter interface before the genomic insert is subjected to bisulfite conversion.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Adapter-completed DNA is treated with bisulfite, changing susceptible unmethylated cytosines so that subsequent amplification and sequencing can report C-to-T conversion. This is a conversion of the genomic DNA library substrate, not methylated-DNA capture.
operations.mechanism: Sodium-bisulfite treatment follows methylated adapter replacement and gap repair. The catalogue describes the resulting sequencing-level conversion of unmethylated cytosines to thymidines.
operations.information_effect: Cytosine-modification information becomes readable through the converted genomic sequence. The readout cannot distinguish 5mC from 5hmC, so a protected signal is not uniquely specific to 5mC.
